name: Catalog Launch Guard
description: Audit every catalog record before launch, separate confirmed blockers from legitimate merchandising structures, and publish an evidence-backed red/amber/green dashboard plus CEO page brief. Read-only against Fluid; no automatic merge, delete, repricing, or publish action.

steps.name: Capture complete catalog
steps.prompt:
Capture a fresh, complete, read-only catalog evidence set for the active company. This is a launch audit, not an import.

Artifact contract (applies to this step): all run artifacts live under the run's artifact directory; every count, list, percentage, and hash you report must be printed by a verification script executed with `run_cli` as `npm exec --yes -- node <script>` — model-recalled or hand-counted numbers are a defect. Scripts must be created with `write_file`, read only saved artifact files, and follow this skeleton: (a) write EXACTLY one JSON object to a summary file (e.g. `<artifact_dir>/verify-summary.json`) and read it back with `read_file` — never parse run_cli's merged stdout/stderr stream; the object is `{"ok":true,...}` with exit 0, or `{"ok":false,"error":{code,message}}` with `process.exit(1)`, and consumers gate on `ok`, never on the mere presence of numbers; (b) refuse to report on data that is not there: assert a minimum expected row count and cross-check any declared count in the input against rows actually parsed — zero defects on zero or partial rows is an ERROR, never a pass; (c) cap every id list at 20 and the field inventory at 200, each with `total` and `truncated` flags, full lists to sibling artifact files; (d) emit an `integrity` block (input file sha256, byte size, declared vs observed row counts) so later steps can prove they reasoned over the same snapshot; (e) be idempotent — reruns must produce byte-identical summaries. If `npm exec` is unavailable, report that as a data gap and stop the affected check — never fall back to hand-counting. Permitted tools for audit work: `read_file`, `write_file`, `list_dir`, `search_files`, `run_cli` (npm/git only), `fluid_catalog_index`, documented v202604 GETs via `fluid_api`, and `query_docs`; do not probe other tools or undocumented paths.

1. Determine the run artifact directory first: let `RUN_PREFIX` be `context.run_prefix` when the caller supplies it, otherwise mint `clg-<UTC now as YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>`. Every artifact this run writes lives under `<RUN_PREFIX>/` (for example `<RUN_PREFIX>/index.json`). Emit `run_prefix` and `artifact_dir` in STEP_OUTPUT so later steps reuse it.
2. Read optional caller `context.catalog_expectations` when present. Supported expectations are `minimum_bundle_count`, `required_phrases` (array), `allowed_zero_price_title_patterns` (array), and `minimum_subscription_product_count`. Treat absent keys as `not specified`, never as zero. These are merchant expectations, not universal rules.
3. Call `query_docs` for the April 2026 company Product list/detail response before assuming fields. Then call `fluid_catalog_index` once with `output_path: "<RUN_PREFIX>/index.json"` and `verify_only: false`. Require `complete: true`, `next_cursor: null`, zero duplicate ids, first/middle/last detail receipts, and the file SHA-256. This tool proves IDENTITY completeness; it does not capture audit fields.
4. Capture full bodies yourself: cursor-paginate `GET /api/v202604/company/products` with `fluid_api`, following every returned `meta.pagination.next_cursor` until null — never stop from a page count or `total_count`. Use the largest page size the endpoint accepts (try `page[limit]=100` first; record the size that actually worked). After EACH page, save that page's `products` array verbatim with `write_file` to `<RUN_PREFIX>/pages/page-<NN>.json` before requesting the next page. Use the documented detail endpoint only for fields the list omits on records you later need to inspect; save any detail responses you fetch to `<RUN_PREFIX>/details/<id>.json`.
5. Create `<RUN_PREFIX>/clg-verify.mjs` with `write_file` and run it. The script must read `<RUN_PREFIX>/index.json` and every `<RUN_PREFIX>/pages/*.json`, then print/persist: row, unique-id, and duplicate-id counts; an exact two-way id-set reconciliation between the walked pages and the index (exit 1 on any delta); lifecycle counts (by `status` and `active`, sellable vs not); ids with missing or zero price per currency; ids missing `image_url` or resized versions; groups of two or more products sharing an identical `image_url` (placeholder detection); duplicate non-empty SKU groups with lifecycle; normalized-title duplicate groups with per-currency price spread; `field_inventory` as the exact union of JSON key paths across every captured record (label it as computed from the captured list pages plus any saved details); and a SHA-256 for every artifact file including itself. Write the full aggregates to `<RUN_PREFIX>/aggregates.json`; stdout carries the capped summary only.
6. Do not change products, variants, prices, bundles, plans, images, or lifecycle. Do not infer a missing business concept from an absent response field.

End with `STEP_OUTPUT:` containing `run_prefix`, `artifact_dir`, `index_path`, `index_sha256`, `aggregates_path`, `aggregates_sha256`, `verify_script_path`, `observed_at`, `pages`, `page_size_used`, `row_count`, `unique_id_count`, `duplicate_id_count`, `reconciliation_delta`, `lifecycle_counts`, `field_inventory_source`, `unavailable_fields`, `expectations`, and `evidence_ready: true|false`. Cap every list at 20 ids and reference the artifact file holding the full list.
acceptance: `fluid_catalog_index` independently proves a terminal null cursor, complete identity set, zero duplicate ids, first/middle/last detail receipts, and a SHA-256 for the run-prefixed index file.

Full product bodies are persisted page-by-page under the run's `pages/` directory, and a committed, re-runnable verification script proves an exact two-way id-set match between the walked pages and the index (reconciliation delta zero, script exit code 0).

Every count, list, and percentage in the report is script output over the saved artifacts; `aggregates.json` exists with a SHA-256; and the field inventory is the script-computed union of key paths across the captured records, labeled with exactly that provenance. Verify by reading the saved artifacts and re-deriving spot values — re-walking the live catalog is NOT required and wastes context; at most two live spot-check GETs.
The evidence capture is read-only against Fluid and claims no product, variant, price, bundle, plan, image, or lifecycle change.

steps.name: Audit catalog structure
acceptance: Every captured unique product id is audited exactly once with coverage computed by script over the saved pages (100%); every inventory count is script output, each finding carries the source id and exact observed fields that triggered it, and at most 10 live detail GETs were used.

Duplicate titles, price divergence, zero prices, missing images, bundle/plan absence, and required-text misses remain merchant-review findings unless independent evidence proves a mechanically unlaunchable state.

Price comparisons stay within currency and distinguish one-time/subscription, cadence, variants/options, and package quantity whenever those fields exist; unavailable dimensions are reported. Verify from the saved artifacts and `findings.json` — re-walking the live catalog is NOT required; at most two live spot-check GETs.
No merge, delete, archive, reprice, publish, bundle, plan, media, or other Fluid mutation occurred, and no unsupported avoided-revenue estimate is present.

steps.name: Review flagged records
steps.prompt:
Independently validate the structural audit's flags against product detail records and produce the approval-safe launch queue. Stay read-only.

Read `artifact_dir` and `findings_path` from the structural-audit STEP_OUTPUT and load the full findings from `findings.json` with `read_file` — the STEP_OUTPUT lists are capped samples, the file is the source of truth. Build a deterministic review set of at most 20 products: include every confirmed-blocker candidate when there are 20 or fewer; otherwise take the 20 highest-severity candidates sorted by stable product id. Fill remaining slots with a stratified sample across exact-title duplicates, divergent prices, zero/missing price, missing image, SKU reuse, variant/options, bundle/plan, required-text, and informational clean records. Record the selection rule.

For every selected id, GET the documented v202604 Product detail and re-check the exact trigger in context. Where a canonical route exists, use one bounded read-only `crawl` for each confirmed-blocker candidate up to a maximum of five routes; a route that renders the wrong product, errors, or is blank confirms a route blocker, while a correctly rendered PDP may clear only that route finding.

Classify every sampled flag as:
- `confirmed_blocker`: live detail/route proves the sellable record cannot be purchased or reliably identified;
- `merchant_decision`: the structure is real but intent cannot be known from data;
- `cleared_false_positive`: detail evidence disproves the trigger;
- `unverifiable`: missing field, route, or access prevents judgment.

Calculate sample false-positive rate as `cleared_false_positive / reviewed_flags`, and state it as the two integers plus the fraction (for example `2/18 = 11.1%`) so the arithmetic is checkable. A launch gate may be GREEN only with zero confirmed blockers, zero unverifiable critical candidates, complete evidence, and false-positive rate <=10%. AMBER means merchant decisions/data gaps remain but nothing mechanically blocks launch. RED means one or more confirmed blockers, incomplete catalog evidence, an unverifiable critical candidate, or false-positive rate above 10%.

Never repair findings in this workflow. Produce an approval queue with product id, title, evidence, recommended review action, risk of acting incorrectly, and the exact future write type that would require explicit approval.

Write the complete approval queue to `<artifact_dir>/approval-queue.json`. End with `STEP_OUTPUT:` containing `artifact_dir`, `approval_queue_path`, `selection_rule`, `reviewed_products`, `reviewed_flags`, `confirmed_blockers`, `merchant_decisions`, `cleared_false_positives`, `unverifiable`, `false_positive_rate`, `gate`, `approval_queue`, and `fluid_writes_performed: false`.
acceptance: The deterministic review set contains at most 20 products, covers every critical candidate when possible plus stratified anomaly and clean cases, and records the exact selection rule.

Each reviewed finding is re-opened by documented Product detail GET and classified as confirmed blocker, merchant decision, cleared false positive, or unverifiable with evidence; up to five critical canonical routes are read-only crawled when available.

The false-positive rate is stated as its integer numerator and denominator with the resulting percentage, the GREEN/AMBER/RED rules are applied exactly (<=10% GREEN threshold, RED for incomplete evidence or unverifiable critical candidates), and the full approval queue is persisted to the run's artifact directory.
The approval queue names future write types and risk of acting incorrectly, while this run performs no catalog repair or Fluid mutation.

steps.name: Publish launch dashboard
acceptance: `list_dashboards` shows a saved `Catalog Launch Guard` dashboard with the exact evidence freshness, audit coverage, gate, blocker/decision counts, and false-positive rate from the run's artifact files.

The dashboard includes a visible gate reason, risk breakdown, lifecycle breakdown (live vs archived), approval table, full dimension-coverage card, and data-quality warning, with every number traceable to the artifact files, without invented revenue or hidden unavailable evidence.

The under-350-word CEO brief exists at the run's `brief.md` with all seven required sections, defers the runtime value to the final gate rather than inventing one, uses verified coverage/counts, and does not claim anomalies are errors or repairs are complete.
STEP_OUTPUT carries `brief_path` instead of inlined brief text, and `fluid_writes_performed` is false — the local dashboard and run artifacts were the only state changes.

steps.name: Review launch gate
acceptance: The verification scripts re-run with exit code 0 and reproduce every dashboard, brief, and STEP_OUTPUT tally exactly; the verify-only re-index either matches step 1's SHA-256 and id set, or the delta is reported as a freshness finding that downgrades the gate to AMBER rather than silently passing or hard-failing.

Live Product GETs reproduce every confirmed blocker plus at least five merchant decisions when available, and the final GREEN/AMBER/RED decision follows the authored thresholds exactly without elevating a duplicate title, zero price, price difference, or missing relationship into a confirmed error without evidence.

`brief-final.md` exists, matches `brief.md` except the filled `More for less` runtime line, and that value is labeled as the wall-clock run window including QA and review time — never as pure compute time or an invented speed multiplier.
`fluid_writes_performed` is false and the handoff requires explicit approval before any product, variant, price, bundle, plan, media, or lifecycle write.
